data.narrative:
Tevel Aerobotics is a Series B-stage drone and autonomous systems company that has raised $42.6M to date. The valuation universe comprises eight private peers in the Drones & Autonomous sector, including Joby Aviation, Zipline, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and Elroy Air. No direct public comparables exist in this narrow category.

The valuation analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, which is applicable given the company's clear Series B positioning. Using total capital raised of $43M as a proxy baseline, a 1.9x step-up multiplier—standard for Series B to next-stage advancement—yields an implied valuation of $81M. A peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient granular comparables within tight filtering criteria (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier): while five same-sector peers exist, none met the three-datapoint threshold required for reliable median construction. Applying all-sector medians would introduce unacceptable noise.

The triangulated valuation range is $69M (low), $81M (median), and $93M (high). The single-method result introduces material uncertainty around this midpoint. Key sensitivities include the accuracy of the 1.9x multiplier in current market conditions, the company's revenue trajectory and unit economics relative to the peer set, and whether Tevel's specific drone application (precision agriculture) commands a valuation premium or discount versus broader mobility and logistics use cases. Acquisition of additional comparable data or revenue-based methods would strengthen conviction.
